workItems.title: Implement security, permissions, and exposure boundaries
workItems.acceptanceCriteria: Positive and negative access paths enforce the approved security and visibility model. Production human sign-in reaches management through independently validated human/delegated identity. An operator without a grant cannot borrow the portal application's broader privilege. Development identity is rejected by production configuration. Altering an environment, application ID, cursor, operation reference or URL cannot disclose or change an unauthorized resource. Direct server-action/API calls receive the same protection as the visible UI. Reported identity, instance presence, historical health and resource-owner observations retain their source/time distinctions. The portal neither calls another workload's self-control API nor grants/releases execution authority. Session expiry, sign-out, user switching or grant loss blocks pending writes and clears affected protected data. A revoked lookup cannot reveal the result or cause a replacement mutation; only a same-user minimal receipt may remain. Late responses cannot repopulate the previous user's or environment's view. Configuration validation/preview has no publication effect. Publication preserves the reviewed exact payload, creates immutable content, and release creation pins exact authorized sources without assigning them automatically. A state or permission change after preview is checked at commit. A conflict preserves a permitted draft for revised review and does not resubmit automatically. Management is unavailable while a valid session has a prior snapshot. The portal dates and marks the snapshot, disables new changes and queues nothing; reconnect refreshes state before a fresh explicit submission. Unauthorized sensitive fields are absent from browser responses, rendered diffs, logs and error messages. A redaction marker cannot be submitted as a preserved hidden value. Register trigger/job definitions and inspect disabled configuration without starting handlers or performing provider work. Managed activation waits for required authenticated bootstrap and reconciliation. Unselected applications preserve existing behaviour. Source requirements: INT01, INT03, CORE01–03, CORE07. Register jobs in two different application scopes and a shared category. An event can invoke only its authorized exact registered target; category or payload claims cannot select another service's handler. Source requirements: CORE03, CORE10, ID03–04. Submit a callback/custom event through the programmatic port and existing RM04 adapter. Authenticate its owner, retain original identity after an uncertain response, recover identical replay and reject conflicting payload/provenance. Source requirements: CORE08–09, CORE18–19, CORE24–25. Execute a calendar, callback and manual run using real authenticated workload evidence. Creator, producer, requester, executor and reported instance remain separate; forged caller/identity fields cannot establish execution authority. Source requirements: ID01–04, HIST04, HIST08. Close Management admission during active work. Already entered finite work can settle under its independent rules; new attempts, acquisitions and continuous iterations wait. A restarted instance cannot bootstrap from cached permission. Reconciliation precedes resumption. Source requirements: CORE32, CORE36, HIST11. Run task now with two tasks sharing a trigger. Only the selected task receives the manual occurrence. Repeating the same command recovers that run; disabled or unauthorized targets refuse it. Ordinary retry retains the existing run identity. Source requirements: CORE25, CORE31, UI21. Deliver duplicate, lower-sequence, conflicting and delayed reports. Stale progress cannot restore ownership or overwrite current state; authorized late evidence of the original commit can resolve the same unknown run while preserving earlier facts. Source requirements: HIST08–09. Validate bounded progress/result schemas, summary-size limits, unknown totals, protected result references and record-level history authorization. An authorized producer can recover its acceptance without unauthorized target identities, counts or details being disclosed. Reporting distinguishes occurred time, receipt time, known duration and stale observation. Source requirements: CORE24, HIST03–04, HIST12–14. Show the default inherited execution identity, reject unsupported alternatives/delegation and revalidate identity after job selection changes. Remapping a profile alias cannot change an existing run's captured identity, while credential rotation for the same identity remains supported. Policy publication alone does not pretend that an unrestarted instance has new grants or a new principal. Source requirements: ID05–08, UI11, UI16. Open separate task History and run-attempt details without adding a third contextual configuration tab. Show captured requester/producer/executor identities and actual outcome/freshness, with access-sensitive content protected. Source requirements: UI11, HIST14, HIST18. Build and run impacted existing consumers and contract cases. Preserve public compatibility, original transaction ownership, local bounds, Configuration remap behaviour and unselected module startup. Portable C# and TypeScript clients expose the required authenticated operation groups and agree on supported results and large integer representations. Source requirements: INT01, INT06, CORE38, UI19–20. Maintain a consumer example using the central calendar and one application-produced trigger, two Scheduled Tasks sharing a registered job, authenticated multi-instance execution and durable outcome recovery. Its setup, actual provider requirements and supported operating modes are documented. Source requirements: INT02–04, CORE01–09, HIST10. Force an old worker to stop around real transaction completion and notification loss. A compatible replacement reconciles the original operation and preserves one logical run, its actual original outcome and build provenance. Unknown results remain unresolved; deployment neither resets retry allowance nor grants a stale owner permission to commit. Source requirements: VER02, VER06, CORE28–31. workItems.acceptanceCriteria: Backend behavior satisfies positive, negative, state-transition, and concurrency requirements. Register trigger/job definitions and inspect disabled configuration without starting handlers or performing provider work. Managed activation waits for required authenticated bootstrap and reconciliation. Unselected applications preserve existing behaviour. Source requirements: INT01, INT03, CORE01–03, CORE07. Register jobs in two different application scopes and a shared category. An event can invoke only its authorized exact registered target; category or payload claims cannot select another service's handler. Source requirements: CORE03, CORE10, ID03–04. Activate an event-driven Scheduled Task without inventing calendar metadata. Existing external-occurrence and legacy calendar consumers remain compatible through documented adapters. Source requirements: CORE06, CORE08, CORE38. Run at least two Management instances against the same real store and evaluate the same due instant, including a crash at the commit boundary. Exactly one canonical event and its complete selected run set remain; cursor advancement loses no accepted work. Source requirements: INT02, CORE12, CORE17, CORE20. Exercise Daily and Weekly evaluation with explicit zones, unavailable zone, a nonexistent local time and a repeated local time. Results follow Skip and OnceAtEarlierInstant, and preview agrees with production evaluation. Source requirements: CORE11–12, UI10. Change an active schedule around a due boundary; pause and resume unchanged schedules under Skip, RunLatestOnce and CatchUpBounded. Committed instants do not duplicate; old pending runs remain; catch-up obeys its finite window and batch. Source requirements: CORE13–14, CORE33. Exercise FixedDelay initial delay, explicit immediate start, predecessor retries, delay edits, disabled designated task, closed admission, terminal failure/cancellation, explicit resume and unknown outcome. Retain at most one successor without a zero-run dead end or catch-up cycles. Only the designated logical predecessor advances the trigger; extra task association is refused; a manual run does not advance it. Source requirements: CORE14–16. Submit a callback/custom event through the programmatic port and existing RM04 adapter. Authenticate its owner, retain original identity after an uncertain response, recover identical replay and reject conflicting payload/provenance. Source requirements: CORE08–09, CORE18–19, CORE24–25. Fan one event into several tasks. Inject one mapping error and one capacity failure before commitment. Whole admission is refused without partial runs or acknowledgement; valid admission records the complete set. Boundary fan-out and byte limits are enforced. Source requirements: CORE10, CORE20, CORE37, OPS01. Accept an event with no enabled matching task, then add or enable a task and redeliver that event. The original zero-run receipt remains authoritative. A previously unaccepted event uses the task set active at first successful acceptance. Source requirements: CORE19, CORE21–22, CORE34. Edit task, mapper and shared configuration after event acceptance, then redeliver or recover its runs. Original task selection, identities, input and captured runtime/business settings remain unchanged. Source requirements: CORE19, CORE23, UI14–15. Use a handler that reads the typed captured business settings while the ordinary live Configuration root adopts a newer value. The existing root keeps its normal semantics; the old run still receives its original settings. Source requirements: CORE23, UI15. Pause a trigger, disable a task, disable a job/category and retire a task. Observe the distinct production/admission/execution effects; retained pending responsibility and receipt recovery survive. CIS produces a visible, versioned design package with complete inspection/change journeys and API mappings. An unapproved or rejected design blocks production UI tasks. An approval survives restart for the unchanged design. A material changed workflow requires approval of that revision; routine presentation fixes do not prompt again. Production human sign-in reaches management through independently validated human/delegated identity. An operator without a grant cannot borrow the portal application's broader privilege. Development identity is rejected by production configuration. Altering an environment, application ID, cursor, operation reference or URL cannot disclose or change an unauthorized resource. Direct server-action/API calls receive the same protection as the visible UI. Missing or incompatible capability versions are unavailable truthfully. Unknown response states never default to success, and opaque inventory detail is rendered safely. Cross-page application filtering uses the documented server query. Cursors bind the query/scope; changing filters resets them. No loaded page is advertised as a fleet-wide count or complete environment list. Reported identity, instance presence, historical health and resource-owner observations retain their source/time distinctions. The portal neither calls another workload's self-control API nor grants/releases execution authority. Metadata editing affects only supported display fields. Concurrent edits preserve the strong ETag contract; the losing edit is reviewed against current state rather than silently overwriting it. A mutation commits but its response is lost, then the page reloads. Recovery uses the original key and validated actor/target, performs one effect and one required audit, and preserves committed/rejected/unknown and cleanup distinctions. Session expiry, sign-out, user switching or grant loss blocks pending writes and clears affected protected data. A revoked lookup cannot reveal the result or cause a replacement mutation; only a same-user minimal receipt may remain. Late responses cannot repopulate the previous user's or environment's view. Configuration validation/preview has no publication effect. Publication preserves the reviewed exact payload, creates immutable content, and release creation pins exact authorized sources without assigning them automatically. A state or permission change after preview is checked at commit. A conflict preserves a permitted draft for revised review and does not resubmit automatically. Canary promotion and rollback show every affected default/cohort entry. Promotion handles the override explicitly; rollback advances assignment generation and retains immutable publication history. Mixed Applied, AppliedUnchanged, Pending, Rejected, PendingRestart and Faulted observations remain distinct from stale/offline status. Zero observed recipients and outdated successful reports are not called converged. Management is unavailable while a valid session has a prior snapshot. Unauthorized sensitive fields are absent from browser responses, rendered diffs, logs and error messages. A redaction marker cannot be submitted as a preserved hidden value. Large Int64 strings, exact ETags, prefixed URLs, unknown fields/statuses and response limits retain existing cross-language behavior through the UI and Next.js integration. Keyboard-only and narrow/zoomed principal journeys preserve labels, target visibility, focus, error recovery and result access. Representative rendered screens match the approved design. Render owner-described fields and a calendar editor using trusted descriptors. Conflicting schema versions, unsupported mapper/editor identifiers, executable form content and untrusted lookup targets cannot activate invalid configuration. Source requirements: UI01–06, UI17. Publish a draft affecting multiple owners and inject a partial failure, uncertain response and concurrent edit. Recover original successful operations, retain the draft on conflict and show pending/active/adopted states accurately. Shared edits revalidate all affected tasks, including tasks outside the current editor, without overwriting newer edits. New event admission sees a coherent compatible active revision; existing runs retain their captured settings. Source requirements: UI12–18. Show the default inherited execution identity, reject unsupported alternatives/delegation and revalidate identity after job selection changes. Remapping a profile alias cannot change an existing run's captured identity, while credential rotation for the same identity remains supported. Policy publication alone does not pretend that an unrestarted instance has new grants or a new principal. Source requirements: ID05–08, UI11, UI16. Open separate task History and run-attempt details without adding a third contextual configuration tab. Show captured requester/producer/executor identities and actual outcome/freshness, with access-sensitive content protected. Source requirements: UI11, HIST14, HIST18. Reconcile the actual checkout and component ownership, import this specification through supported CIS traceability, and deliver the required adapters, clients, consumer guidance and migration instructions. Record focused acceptance evidence against the qualified commit and disclose material gaps. Preserve the accepted editor; obtain existing RM09 approval only for uncovered visual decisions. Source requirements: UI22, UI24, DEL01–05. Capture actual application/build/handler metadata before an attempt can enter business execution. A forged event version cannot substitute it, a later catalog update cannot rewrite it, and a new build recovering an old result preserves the original effect attribution. History distinguishes mixed-version attempts and explicitly unknown provenance. Source requirements: VER01–03, VER09, HIST04, HIST07. Activate a newer job execution contract while old runs remain queued or unresolved. New runs capture the new active contract; old runs retain theirs. When supporting workers disappear, show a bounded version-related waiting reason without consuming retries or changing run state to a fabricated failure. The Job and History views remain within the accepted layout. Source requirements: VER03–04, VER09, UI14–15. This task covers its accepted scope, exclusions and dependencies.
